introduction.text: In the first sentence, say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank and that the call is recorded.
introduction.source: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded

rules.text: Before identity is verified, do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product.
rules.source: Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified.

rules.text: The restriction on what may be said before verification applies to everyone, including relatives.
rules.source: This applies to everyone, including relatives.

rules.text: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
rules.source: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.

rules.text: If the customer asks whether this is a scam, say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, then continue.
rules.source: say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.

rules.text: If the customer asks a question instead of confirming, answer it first. The confirmation question that follows counts as the second ask.
rules.source: Answer a question from the customer first (rules 4 and 43). The ask that follows is the second ask.

unclear_instruction.text: Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name confirms. For anything else, ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as not_reached / unclear.
unclear_instruction.source: Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.

rules.text: Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence.
rules.source: Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1.

rules.text: Ask when the customer can be reached.
rules.source: Ask when the customer can be reached.

rules.text: Accept a callback only for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00 inclusive, and later than now. Then call schedule_callback with the date and time.
rules.source: A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`.

rules.text: If the person offers a day or time outside the window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule; close as not_reached / no_callback.
rules.source: If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.

rules.text: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as not_reached / deceased.
rules.source: say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.

rules.text: Never let a relative answer the security questions or tell them anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
rules.source: A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.

rules.text: Ask two security questions, one at a time: date of birth first, then the last four digits of the phone number on file.
rules.source: Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file.

rules.text: A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total, on any question, end the check.
rules.source: A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.

rules.text: Read a date of birth given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
rules.source: Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.

rules.text: Do not state the debt or fetch the account until both questions pass.
rules.source: After both questions pass, call `get_account`.

rules.text: If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as not_verified / declined.
rules.source: explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.

rules.text: Treat asking what the call is about instead of answering as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call as not_verified / declined.
rules.source: Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.

ask.text: Ask for the customer's date of birth.
ask.source: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file

answer_format.text: Convert the spoken date of birth to YYYY-MM-DD, whatever way the customer said it.
answer_format.source: Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it.

ask.text: Ask for the last four digits of the phone number on file.
ask.source: then the last four digits of the phone number on file

failed_answer_instruction.text: After a wrong answer, ask the question again. If verify_identity returns hint day_month_swapped, ask the customer to say the month as a word; this retry is not a wrong answer.
failed_answer_instruction.source: Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.

exhausted_say.text: Do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch, then close as not_verified / failed.
exhausted_say.source: After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch.

rules.text: Say you are calling from the collections team about a late payment.
rules.source: Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment.

rules.text: Name each product in words: credit card ending with its last four digits, personal loan or car loan.
rules.source: Name the product in words:

rules.text: For each product, state the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
rules.source: State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.

rules.text: State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.
rules.source: State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.

rules.text: Go through the products in the order the account tool returned them.
rules.source: in the order `get_account` returned them

rules.text: With one product, first ask: Can you make this payment today?
rules.source: Can you make this payment today?

rules.text: With several products, first ask whether the customer can pay all of them today. If not, go through the products one by one.
rules.source: First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.

rules.text: Do not ask about paying today again for each product.
rules.source: Do not ask about today again for each product.

rules.text: Ask for the full past-due amount first.
rules.source: Ask for the full past-due amount first.

rules.text: Never ask the customer how much they can pay. The agent proposes every amount.
rules.source: The agent proposes every amount.

rules.text: A date or an amount proposed by the customer is never a refusal. Handle it under the date and amount rules.
rules.source: A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal.

rules.text: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
rules.source: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.

rules.text: A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
rules.source: A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.

rules.text: Attempt 1: ask for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
rules.source: Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.

rules.text: Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
rules.source: Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week.

rules.text: Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
rules.source: Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.

rules.text: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor once and say that the rest stays overdue.
rules.source: Say that the rest stays overdue.

rules.text: When the persuasion attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused.
rules.source: When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused.

rules.text: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in the brief.
rules.source: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

rules.text: Count persuasion attempts per product. Start each product at attempt 1.
rules.source: Persuasion attempts are counted per product.

rules.text: Handle the products in account order, one at a time. Each product has its own band and deadline.
rules.source: The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`.

rules.text: If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, handle it first: make no persuasion attempt and do not transfer to restructuring until the hardship path is done.
rules.source: This rule comes before rules 30 and 41.

rules.text: In hardship, if the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under the date and amount rules.
rules.source: If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.

rules.text: Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask: Do you confirm?
rules.source: Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask

rules.text: With several products, read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation.
rules.source: Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation.

rules.text: Call create_promise only after a clear yes.
rules.source: Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.

rules.text: Call create_promise once per product after the confirmation.
rules.source: Then call `create_promise` once per product.

rules.text: If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value and read it back again.
rules.source: If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.

rules.text: If one date for everything is after a product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back. The other products keep the customer's date.
rules.source: record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back.

rules.text: One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in this call. If asked, say they can change it in the mobile app.
rules.source: One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call.

rules.text: Say the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok true.
rules.source: Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`.

rules.text: After a recorded promise, say: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
rules.source: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.

rules.text: If recording fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it.
rules.source: If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it

rules.text: With several products, if one create_promise fails twice, keep the promises already recorded and add a service_error note for the failed product.
rules.source: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded

say.text: Say that payments can take one business day to appear.
say.source: say that payments can take one business day to appear

when.source: If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss

say.text: Say one short sentence of sympathy.
say.source: say one short sentence of sympathy

ask.text: Offer to connect the customer with the customer support team.
ask.source: Offer to connect them with the customer support team.

when.text: The customer in hardship declines the offer to connect with customer support.
when.source: If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.

say.text: Say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt.
say.source: say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt

say.source: do not describe a plan

when.source: at least one promise was recorded

say.text: Say: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise." Then thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."

when.text: The customer says they already paid, and no promise was recorded; with several products, every product is noted paid.
when.source: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`

say.text: Say that payments can take one business day to appear. Then thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: say that payments can take one business day to appear

say.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

say.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

say.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.text: The customer refused, persuasion attempts are used up, or the customer twice said they do not want to talk.
when.source: Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.

say.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.source: If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.

say.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.text: The customer says the debt is not theirs or they never had the product, or says the product was closed or paid off in the past.
when.source: Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.

say.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.text: Recording the promise failed twice.
when.source: say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`

say.text: Say you could not record the promise. Then thank the customer and say goodbye.

when.text: Three wrong security answers in total.
when.source: Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.

say.text: Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Then thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch.

when.text: The customer still declines the security questions after one explanation, or asks what the call is about instead of answering twice.
when.source: If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.

say.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.text: Someone else answered and a callback was booked with schedule_callback.
when.source: Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.

say.text: Thank the person and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.text: Both callback times offered are outside the window, so no callback is scheduled.
when.source: Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.

say.text: Thank the person and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.text: The person says the number does not belong to the customer.
when.source: If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.

say.text: Thank the person and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

when.text: The person says the customer has died.
when.source: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss."

say.text: Say "I am sorry for your loss." Ask nothing else. Then say goodbye.
say.source: say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`

when.text: Who answered is still unclear after the second ask.
when.source: If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.

say.text: Thank the person and say goodbye.
say.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

global_rules.text: Address the customer as title plus last name.
global_rules.source: Address the customer as title plus last name.

global_rules.text: Pass customer_id to every tool call.
global_rules.source: Pass it to every tool call.

global_rules.text: Use the call variable now for every date rule, never the real clock.
global_rules.source: The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock.

global_rules.text: If asked something the tools cannot answer, say you do not have that information. Never invent figures, dates or reasons.
global_rules.source: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.

global_rules.text: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in the brief.
global_rules.source: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

global_rules.text: If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk after identity is verified, close as no_promise / refused.
global_rules.source: If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`.

global_rules.text: If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk before identity is verified, close as not_verified / declined.
global_rules.source: Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`.

global_rules.text: If the customer asks for a human, ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call transfer_to_agent with queue general and close as transferred / human. This applies before and after verification.
global_rules.source: A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first.

global_rules.text: End every call with exactly one close_call, with an outcome and a reason where the table lists one.
global_rules.source: Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason.

global_rules.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye before calling close_call.
global_rules.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

rules.text: End every call with exactly one close_call that has an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason.
rules.source: Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason.

rules.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye before close_call.
rules.source: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

rules.text: If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as transferred with the transfer's reason.
rules.source: If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.

rules.text: If at least one promise was recorded, close as promise (except after a transfer).
rules.source: With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above.

rules.text: If no promise was recorded and every product is noted paid, close as paid.
rules.source: With no promise recorded: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`.

rules.text: If no promise was recorded otherwise, close as no_promise with the reason of the first product in get_account order whose note is not paid.
rules.source: Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`.

rules.text: On any transfer add no notes, before or after it.
rules.source: On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.

rules.text: If one create_promise fails twice, keep the recorded promises and add a service_error note for the failed product.
rules.source: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded and call `add_note` with reason `service_error` for the failed product.

rules.text: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the product's deadline.
rules.source: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

rules.text: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day.
rules.source: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day.

rules.text: If the customer gives a vague period, ask once for the exact day.
rules.source: If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day.

rules.text: If the customer still gives no exact day, propose the deadline.
rules.source: If they still give none, propose the deadline.

rules.text: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week.
rules.source: means that weekday in the following calendar week.

rules.text: "This <weekday>" means that weekday in the current week.
rules.source: "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week.

rules.text: If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it.
rules.source: say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it.

rules.text: If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal.
rules.source: If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

rules.text: With several products, if one date is named for everything and it is after a product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back.
rules.source: record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back.

rules.text: Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask how much the customer can pay.
rules.source: Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?".

rules.text: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor once and say the rest stays overdue.
rules.source: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue.

rules.text: Accept any amount from the floor up to the full past-due amount, both included.
rules.source: If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.

rules.text: If the amount is below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
rules.source: Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.

rules.text: If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal.
rules.source: If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

rules.text: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in the brief.
rules.source: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

provenance.opening.max_unclear_asks: If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.
provenance.opening.forbidden_before_verification: Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified.
provenance.agent.language: fallback: the documents name no call language; English, because every sentence the agent must say is written in English.
provenance.confirmation.max_attempts_per_product: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded
provenance.offer.rules: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
provenance.offer.today_variable: All date rules use this, never the real clock.
provenance.offer.non_business_weekdays: Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
provenance.offer.holidays: Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
provenance.offer.promise_date_must_be_business_day: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
provenance.offer.earliest: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
provenance.offer.latest: | 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |
provenance.offer.latest_on_non_business_day: fallback: deadlines are counted in business days, so they always fall on a business day; no calendar-day latest date in the documents
provenance.offer.min_amount: The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
provenance.offer.max_amount: If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.
provenance.offer.next_weekday: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week.
provenance.offer.max_rejected_offers: fallback: no invalid-offer limit in the documents
provenance.offer.max_rejected_offers_by_product: fallback: no invalid-offer limit in the documents, so no per-product limits
provenance.say.goodbye: The briefs give no goodbye wording, only 'Thank the customer and say goodbye' (rule 47). Rows without a fixed sentence use that instruction.
provenance.special_paths.human_request.say: The brief fixes no sentence for the human transfer, so the general goodbye instruction (rule 47) is used.
provenance.special_paths.restructuring.say: The brief fixes no sentence, only that no plan may be described.
provenance.special_paths.hardship.say: The brief fixes no sympathy wording, only 'one short sentence of sympathy'.
provenance.special_paths.dispute.say: The brief fixes no sentence for a dispute, only 'do not argue'.
provenance.special_paths.already_paid_and_dispute.t: Brief B rule 9 says a dispute or an already-paid claim on one product does not end the call, so these paths return. The closing is then computed from the notes.
provenance.special_paths.add_note: product_id is filled by the conversation. add_note is Brief B only. No notes are added on transfers (Brief B rule 10).
provenance.outcomes.paid.when: Rule 39 sets the paid outcome when no promise exists. Brief B closes as paid when every product is noted paid.
provenance.states: The required and optional states are each mapped to exactly one row.
provenance.outcomes.state.callback_failed: derived: No callback could be booked. The closest row is not_reached / no_callback, because no callback exists.
provenance.outcomes.state.account_failed: derived: A technical failure on get_account is closest to the service error row, no_promise / service_error.
provenance.outcomes.state.offer_limit: derived: The brief treats failing offers as a flat refusal, so no_promise / refused.
provenance.outcomes.state.turn_limit: derived: No progress means no promise and no stated reason, so the generic refusal row, no_promise / refused.
provenance.outcomes.state.special_tool_failed: derived: A failed special tool means the action could not be done, so no_promise / service_error.
provenance.outcomes.state.hangup: derived: A verified customer who leaves without a promise is treated as a refusal, no_promise / refused.
provenance.outcomes.state.hangup_unverified: derived: Leaving before identity is verified is treated as not answering the questions, not_verified / declined.
provenance.outcomes.state.default: derived: Any other end with no promise uses the generic refusal row, no_promise / refused.

overrides.effect: Brief B notes every product that ended without a promise using add_note.

overrides.newer: A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call.
overrides.effect: A dispute on one product is noted and the call continues with the other products. The closing outcome is derived from the notes.

overrides.newer: A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call.
overrides.older: take no promise, and close as `paid`

overrides.newer: The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`.
overrides.older: The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
overrides.effect: Each product has its own band and deadline.

overrides.newer: First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today.
overrides.older: First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
overrides.effect: With several products the first ask covers all products, then the products are handled one by one.
